newsitem.title: RUSSIA: At least one killed in Russian rail station blast.
newsitem.headline: At least one killed in Russian rail station blast.

text.p: An explosion rocked a railway station in southern Russia on Monday, killing one person and injuring 12, an Emergencies Ministry spokesman said.

He said the first-floor blast had blown out all the windows of the station in Pyatigorsk, 130 km (80 miles) northwest of the breakaway Chechnya region from where radical separatists have vowed to attack targets in southern Russia.
Interfax and RIA news agencies later said two people had been killed, but the reports could not immediately be confirmed.
Itar-Tass news agency quoted Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov as saying the blast had "Chechen links".
Two people were killed in a bomb blast at another southern Russian railway station last Wednesday at Armavir, about 190 km (120 miles) northwest of Pyatigorsk.
The spokesman said it was not immediately known what caused Monday evening's blast at Pyatigorsk, in the north Caucasus mountains, which was part of the same rail network as Armavir.
"We can say for sure that one person was killed. Twelve were taken to hospital," he said. "We do not have any details of how powerful the explosion was."

Radical separatist guerrilla commander Salman Raduyev has vowed to attack Russia's rail network and other targets to press Chechnya's campaign for independence even though a 21-month-long conflict with Russian troops ended last August.
Itar-Tass news agency said Raduyev claimed responsibility for last week's explosion at Armavir, but Chechen leaders later said they doubted he was behind the attack.
Chechen leaders are demanding full independence for their mainly Moslem region but Moscow has ruled this out.
